comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4, C52, C55-C59 regarding the modification site and linkage chemistry. Both evaluations find this characterization well-supported by experimental evidence including chemical treatments and site-specific modifications.

Perfect agreement on claims C72-C77 regarding kinetic comparison between F-NAD+ and ssNA substrates. Both acknowledge this quantitative comparison as supported, with OpenEval noting the incomplete saturation caveat and peer reviewers recognizing this addresses concerns about physiological relevance of direct ssNA ubiquitination.

Perfect agreement on claims C85-C90 regarding DTX3L/DTX3 specificity among family members. Both evaluations find the comparative studies, trans-complementation, and chimera experiments well-supported and acknowledge this as an important finding about unique domain architecture.

Strong agreement on claims C8, C79, C82-C83 regarding DTC domain mutational analysis. Both find the evidence for catalytic role of conserved residues supported by the biochemical characterization, though OpenEval notes additional structural data would strengthen mechanistic inferences.

Strong agreement on claims C61-C66 regarding substrate specificity requirements. Both evaluations accept the systematic characterization of nucleotide sequences, lengths, and structural configurations as well-supported and thorough.

Strong agreement on core finding (claims C1, C36-C37, C39, C43-C44, C110) that DTX3L directly ubiquitinates ssNAs. Both evaluations find this novel discovery well-supported by multiple complementary experiments. Peer review explicitly affirms this represents 'solid evidence' and 'significant expansion of ubiquitin biology.'

Agreement on mechanistic model (claims C91-C92). Both find the proposed mechanism reasonable based on collective biochemical evidence, though peer reviewers note that physiological substrates and functionally relevant sites remain to be established.

Partial disagreement on claims C7, C67-C69, C84 regarding DTC domain binding interface. OpenEval finds NMR and competition data well-supported for overlapping binding sites. Peer reviewers accept the competition data but specifically critique that binding interface details are not mapped onto structure, requesting more complete structural characterization.
Agreement on claims C6, C48 regarding USP2 reversibility and nucleic acid involvement. Both evaluations accept this as part of the overall biochemical characterization without concerns.

Agreement on claims C47, C50 regarding component requirements and distinction from ADP-ribose ubiquitination. Both find these mechanistic characterization experiments supported and note they address important questions about reaction specificity.

Agreement on claims C95, C97 regarding N-terminal domain characterization and RD region binding contribution. Both evaluations accept the domain mapping and binding experiments, though note the precise functional roles remain incompletely understood.

Agreement on claims C2-C3, C34 regarding RD domain as minimal catalytic unit and N-terminal domain predictions. Both find the domain deletion experiments and structural predictions well-supported as part of the overall characterization.

Significant disagreement on claim C105 regarding poly-A ssRNA ubiquitination and physiological relevance. OpenEval finds this supported with potential biological relevance. Peer reviewers express 'healthy skepticism about physiological significance' and note inability to detect modification in cells, characterizing work as 'starting point' for establishing physiological relevance.

Agreement on claim C110 regarding novelty of direct ssNA ubiquitination. Both evaluations acknowledge this as a novel finding distinct from prior work on ADP-ribosylated nucleic acids, with peer reviewers calling it 'significant expansion of ubiquitin biology.'

Divergent focus on background claims C101-C104. OpenEval categorizes these as appropriately cited literature providing context. Peer reviewers group these with C105 in expressing uncertainty about physiological relevance and noting absence of cellular detection.

OpenEval finds claim C45 regarding time-course kinetics supported as straightforward enzymatic observation. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though implicitly accepted as part of overall biochemical characterization.

OpenEval finds claims C53-C54 regarding chemical treatment experiments supported as validation of ester bond chemistry. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though implicitly accepted within overall site mapping characterization.

OpenEval rates claims C106-C109 as UNCERTAIN, noting that while structural differences are documented, claim C109 about functional significance of extended groove is speculative without experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these structural predictions.
